drivingQuestion: Why may the High Priest not perform yibbum with a widow from betrothal?
outcomeNote: the difficulty is completed in the next unit

segments.he: חוֹלֵץ וְחוֹלְצִין כּוּ׳. קָא פָּסֵיק וְתָנֵי, לָא שְׁנָא מִן הָאֵירוּסִין וְלָא שְׁנָא מִן הַנִּישּׂוּאִין. בִּשְׁלָמָא מִן הַנִּישּׂוּאִין, הָוֵי עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה -
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that the High Priest «performs ḥalitza» with his brother’s widow «and» his brother «performs ḥalitza» with his wife, but in any case he does not consummate levirate marriage with his brother’s wife. The Gemara comments: The mishna «categorically teaches» that the High Priest does not consummate levirate marriage, and there «is no difference» whether his brother’s wife was a widow «from betrothal» alone «and no difference» whether she was a widow «from a marriage» that had been consummated. «Granted,» it is understood that he does not consummate levirate marriage with a widow «from marriage,» since «there is» both «a positive mitzva:» “And he shall take a wife in her virginity” (Leviticus 21:13), «and» also «a prohibition:» “A widow, or one divorced, or a ḥalala, or a zona, these shall he not take” (Leviticus 21:14),

moves.summary: no distinction between betrothal and marriage
moves.about: the ban on yibbum applies whether the widow is from betrothal or marriage
